clue.text: Battles in passage a month in advance

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the battles go inside the passage

parts.note: a ford is a passage across a river
battles make up a war
this part belongs to the 26 light, which reads 'See 1': a month is the word that follows in the full command

explanation.surface: An army fights its way through a narrow pass, moving on a month ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The light pairs with 26 to make the drill order, and it also finishes the phrase begun at 16 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward and in advance both describe a position ahead of the others or toward the front.

clue.text: Donêt give food to those who drink outside breakfast time?

indicators.note: the drinkers stand outside, wrapped around the time of day

parts.note: to drink like a fish is to drink heavily, so fish are those who drink
breakfast is eaten in the morning, abbreviated AM

explanation.surface: Advice not to feed people who were drinking before breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: To drink like a fish is a stock idiom for heavy drinking. The odd character in the first word is the source's mangled apostrophe in 'Don't'.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish someone is to starve them, depriving them of nourishment until they are desperately hungry.

clue.text: Diet and exercise for the government

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a planned course of healthy living
second meaning: the ruling administration of a country

explanation.surface: A fitness plan is proposed for the nation's rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a prescribed plan of eating and training and a system or period of rule.

clue.text: I agree with you — all bets off!

definitions.text: I agree with you — all bets off!

parts.words: I agree with you — all bets off!
parts.note: surface reading: someone concedes the point so completely that there is nothing left to wager on
setter's reading: a reply that admits no doubt at all, an unconditional yes with no hedging, so no bet is needed

explanation.surface: One party in a dispute concedes the point and calls off the wager.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is a sample of the answer in use: total agreement, with no conditions left to bet on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an emphatic yes, signalling complete and unqualified agreement with what was said.

clue.text: Money put first in passage

indicators.note: to put something in a place sets it inside, here inside the passage

parts.note: a duct is a channel or passage for liquid or air
A is the first letter and the mark for first class

explanation.surface: Cash is the first thing to be stashed in a hidden passage.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes between DUC and T.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe for centuries, so it serves as money.

clue.text: Green activity with one's 17 22, 24 14, and 16 1across

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a golfer does on the green, tapping the ball toward the hole

definitions.note: the gerund that goes before each of the linked phrases
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the verb that heads the three idioms for setting to work

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references spell out shoulder to the wheel, hand to the plough and best foot forward, and each idiom begins with this verb plus one's.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers perform this stroke on the green, and it also introduces the stock phrases about applying oneself energetically.

clue.text: Page in black and white paper? It will never happen

indicators.note: the page is set in the middle of the black-and-white word

parts.note: pied means patched in black and white, like a magpie
P is the standard abbreviation for page
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper printed in black and white wonders about something that will never come about.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful hope or plan that has no realistic chance of coming true, originally an opium smoker's fantasy.

clue.text: Minor branch of knowledge?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small shoot off a tree

definitions.note: a noun cluing the verb meaning to come to understand
definitions.meaning: second meaning: informal British verb for catching on or grasping

explanation.surface: A minor academic subject, a small branch of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an obscure field of study; the word is both a small branch and slang for understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A twig is a slender shoot of a tree, and in British slang to twig something is to realise it.

clue.text: Setter by himself with some guest that is equivalent but not identical

definitions.note: describes the noun, a compound similar to another

indicators.note: only some of the visitor is used, so the word is cut short

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
alone, on one's own
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter, alone apart from a guest, ponders things that match without being the same.
explanation.walkthrough: GUEST loses its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an isologue is a compound with a similar structure to another though differing in some atoms, so alike yet distinct.

clue.text: Hung out with model holding illustration of the battle for the West

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside
hung out suggests laundry spread about, so its letters are scattered

parts.note: anagram fodder
the Model T was Ford's famous early car
fig. is short for figure, an illustration in a book

explanation.surface: A model poses beside a hanged man as the picture of a Wild West showdown.
explanation.walkthrough: The model is the Model T Ford, a common crossword source of T; the illustration goes in after the first three rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-out with pistols was the classic decisive confrontation of frontier America and of Western films.

clue.text: 'The Wizard', an American periodical?

parts.note: mag is short for magazine
US for United States

explanation.surface: A magazine in the States called The Wizard.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a magazine title; MAG and US come in the order a periodical from the States would be written.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a sorcerer or magician, as in the novel by John Fowles of that title.

clue.text: Sign of grain on an island

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A sign that corn is grown on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, grain 'on' the island is placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn, the goat, is one of the twelve zodiac signs, covering late December to January.

clue.text: Likeness is due to change with the entry of some soldiers

indicators.note: an entry is a going in, so one piece enters the other
a call for change means those letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: only some of the soldiers are wanted, so the word is shortened

parts.note: a militia is a body of citizen soldiers

explanation.surface: A portrait is due to be altered when a troop of soldiers arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: MILITIA loses IA, and the remainder goes inside the rearranged IS DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Similitude is a formal word for resemblance, the quality of being similar to something.

clue.text: Bear a slight 11 to 9?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cartoon bear of Jellystone Park

definitions.note: 11 is likeness and 9 is wizard, so a figure slightly like a wizard
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a Hindu ascetic with mystic powers, a little like a wizard

explanation.walkthrough: Resolve the cross-references: 11 is SIMILITUDE, likeness, and 9 is MAGUS, wizard. Yogi Bear is the Hanna-Barbera cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu holy man practising meditation may seem to have uncanny powers, and Yogi is also a famous cartoon bear.

clue.text: Highland lassie bent nail, keeping things that attract a sultanate

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the attracting things sit inside

parts.note: a claw is a curved, hooked nail
north and south poles of magnets attract each other
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl twists a nail while magnets draw in an Arabian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent nail' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a definition of a hooked nail. N and S, the magnet's poles, go in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman belonging to a Scottish Highland clan, the kinship group of the Highlands.

clue.text: See 24
Brute is on form: he was one of Caesar's killers

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new name

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Brutus is in good form, and so is another of the conspirators who murdered Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: Brute echoes Brutus, Caesar's most famous assassin, pulling the solver toward the wrong conspirator.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaius Trebonius was among the senators who conspired in the assassination on the Ides of March.

clue.text: Get cracking from low down with two and a half footballers

indicators.note: a half means only part of the player's title is used

parts.note: George Best, the Manchester United and Northern Ireland winger
the word itself, to be cut in half
the count of whole players: Best, plus the forward that is the 1 across light

explanation.surface: A coach urges a squad of two and a half players to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second whole footballer is a forward, the 1 across light that ends the phrase; the half is the first half of footballer. The foot is the lowest part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting one's best foot forward means setting off with energy and making a good start on a task.

clue.text: Get cracking from higher up: ought royal child to cut a cad?

parts.note: ought to and should mean the same
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher
a tot is a small child
to hew is to chop
a heel is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a royal child should be allowed to snub a bounder.
explanation.walkthrough: The shoulder is higher on the body than the hand or foot of the companion clues. The phrase runs on into 22 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting one's shoulder to the wheel means applying oneself vigorously to a job, as if pushing a stuck cart.

clue.text: American entertainer causes safe-breaker holding tiller to lose his head

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside
losing a head means the first letter of the burglar goes

parts.note: peter is old slang for a safe, so a peterman cracks safes
the helm is the tiller or wheel that steers a boat

explanation.surface: A burglar grips a boat's tiller and goes so mad that he loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old underworld slang for a safe, so a safe-breaker is a peterman; his head is his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel Merman was the loud-voiced Broadway star of Annie Get Your Gun and Gypsy.

clue.text: Friers give a name 22

definitions.note: a name for the 22 across wheel, the funfair one

indicators.note: to give is to yield or bend out of shape, so the letters shift

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: People who fry things lend their name to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is THE WHEEL, so the definition is a name given to a wheel: the big fairground one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ferris wheel is named after George Ferris, who built the first for the 1893 Chicago fair.

clue.text: Girl who helps to heal the afflicted

indicators.note: the run of words helps to form the name, contributing letters to it

parts.note: the letters run across the first three words

explanation.surface: A girl works as a nurse, caring for the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the name comes from the Greek for healing, and althaea is the marsh mallow, a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Althea is a girl's name, borne for example by the tennis champion Althea Gibson.

clue.text: This strain exemplifies this ology

parts.note: surface reading: a piece of music illustrates some branch of science
setter's reading: put the word before ology and you have saying the same thing twice; tight and strained mean the same, so the pairing is an example

explanation.surface: A tune is held up as a textbook case of an academic discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus ology makes the word for needless repetition, and calling it a strain repeats its own meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight, under strain, so a taut strain says one thing twice.

clue.text: See 17
Army needs a plant

parts.note: a host is a large army or multitude
taken as written

explanation.surface: Military forces require someone planted on the inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosta is a shade-loving garden perennial grown for its broad leaves.

clue.text: Get cracking from midway, within reach (when inverted) of Ursa Major

parts.note: within reach; turned round word by word it becomes the reverse phrase
the Plough is the British name for the seven bright stars of the Great Bear

explanation.surface: Start work from the middle, reaching up toward the Great Bear in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The hand sits midway on the body, between shoulder and foot of the companion clues. The phrase continues at 14 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting one's hand to the plough means committing oneself to a task and getting on with it.

clue.text: Girls once 'ad dollies when upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: anagram fodder, the dropped h ignored

explanation.surface: Grannies remember having dolls as children, upset when they were taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h of 'ad is a Cockney touch to make the fodder fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly women were all young girls at some point in the past, a playful reading of girls once.

clue.text: See 1

definitions.note: the definition and wordplay sit in the 1 across clue

wordplay.note: the words 'a month' in the 1 across clue supply this light, the third month of the year

explanation.walkthrough: Read with 1 across, the two lights make the parade-ground order to advance.
explanation.definitionFit: March is the third calendar month, and forward march is the drill command to step off.

clue.text: Winds enveloping the island cause many, many harsh words

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap around, so the winds surround the island

parts.note: the trades are the trade winds of the tropics
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Storms wrap around an island and provoke a torrent of angry words.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes after the T of TRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches, each made up of many harsh words, hence the doubled many.

clue.text: What elephants don't have, strangely, is a name

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are set out oddly

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that an elephant's lack of forgetfulness is an odd sort of name.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says an elephant never forgets, so elephants lack loss of memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the one thing the proverbial never-forgetting elephant is spared.
